subject.title: fix: keep broken SSH sandbox refs agent-scoped

question: Should SSH lifecycle management preserve the existing inactive-SecretRef contract, or should disabled and mode-off SSH credentials become mandatory runtime-snapshot dependencies?
rationale: The current patch intentionally trades the documented inactive-surface and least-materialization behavior for lifecycle manageability; code correctness alone cannot choose that compatibility and credential-boundary policy.

options.title: Resolve only for lifecycle operations
options.body: Keep inactive refs out of startup, reload, and config-write assignments, and perform targeted fail-closed resolution only when describing or removing a matching SSH runtime.

options.title: Broaden the runtime contract
options.body: Treat configured SSH lifecycle credentials as active even while sandboxing is disabled, then update docs and add explicit fresh-install, upgrade, config-write, reload, and credential-exposure proof.

recommendation.title: Resolve only for lifecycle operations
recommendation.body: Keep inactive refs out of startup, reload, and config-write assignments, and perform targeted fail-closed resolution only when describing or removing a matching SSH runtime.
